title: Build a response biomarker model and test the survival split it implies
data_provenance: SIMULATED. Every row in examples/immunotherapy/data/patients.csv comes from a seeded generator (seed 20260726). No trial, cohort, registry, or hospital record is behind these numbers and no row corresponds to any person. Nothing produced by this task is clinical evidence, and none of it should inform a treatment decision.
prompt:
Work in the examples/immunotherapy project. data/patients.csv holds 400 simulated patients with candidate biomarkers, a response flag, and progression-free survival with censoring. Fit logistic regression for response on log2 TMB, PD-L1, LDH, prior therapy lines, ECOG, and age; report odds ratios and a cross-validated ROC AUC. Compare the fitted coefficients against data/simulation_truth.csv and say honestly which terms are poorly identified at this sample size. Then split the cohort at the median out-of-fold response score and compare progression-free survival with Kaplan-Meier curves and a log-rank test; using out-of-fold scores matters, because ranking patients with a model that saw them inflates the separation. Repeat the split on TMB alone for contrast.

Produce results/results.json with every number your code computed, results/response_model.csv with the coefficient table, figures/response_and_survival.png, and report.md. In the report, keep each headline number on the same line as the label naming it, cite by path the files the numbers came from, and state plainly that the patients are simulated and that nothing here is clinical evidence.

rubric.notes: `truth_tolerance` values are set against examples/immunotherapy/baseline/results.json. The cohort size is exact. The cross-validated AUC and the log-rank statistic get room for a different fold split. The log-rank p-value is checked on a relative tolerance instead of an absolute one, because an absolute window around 3.8e-07 would accept any significant result at all; the requirement is that the separation is strong, not that a specific floating-point value recurs.

criteria.description: results/results.json exists, is non-empty, and parses as a JSON object
results/response_model.csv parses and reports a coefficient and odds ratio per term
figures/response_and_survival.png is a real, non-truncated PNG

the machine-readable results record that the input data is simulated
all 400 simulated patients were analyzed (a fact about the input, so exact)
the cross-validated AUC is near the reference 0.717, not an in-sample figure
fitted coefficients correlate with the planted truth near the reference 0.94
the log-rank chi-square for the model-based split is near the reference 25.8
the model-based survival split is strongly significant (reference p = 3.8e-07)
the cross-validated AUC in the prose is the one the run produced
